page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture with 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Architectural capabilities include hardware virtualization via AMD SVM, cryptographic acceleration with AES and SHA-NI, and advanced vector instructions spanning AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. The instance provides 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU general-purpose ratio, alongside 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, one public IPv4 address, and zero discrete GPUs.

Performance testing reflects strong execution efficiency in compute-focused and memory-intensive metrics. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing workloads. For lightweight AI tasks, text generation using a 135M parameter model also scores in the top decile. In multi-threaded domains, such as multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core scoring, and Clang compilation, the instance delivers steady mid-tier results. Memory subsystems register in the top 25 percent on PassMark memory benchmarks, producing 88.72 GB/s read and 45.8 GB/s write throughput on uncached 256 MB memory blocks.

Resource allocation balances dedicated CPU execution against modest storage boundaries. The dedicated core model prevents host noisy-neighbor interference, delivering predictable multi-tenant isolation and stable compute density. However, the local storage configuration of 1 GB NVMe SSD serves essentially as boot capacity, requiring networked or external block volumes for storage-heavy application architectures. The instance provides balanced cost efficiency for memory-centric and compute-stable workloads, making it well fitted for Redis caching clusters, mid-tier web application servers, Clang software build nodes, and enterprise microservices.
description: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g is a general-purpose cloud instance in the VX1 family, powered by dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, 64.0 GB of memory matching a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio, 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no GPU hardware. The processor features 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instruction sets. Synthetic testing indicates top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng, gzip compression, and text processing, alongside top-decile text generation on lightweight language models. Multi-core performance, static web serving throughput, and Redis key-value operations align within mid-tier categories, while memory tests rank in the top quartile. Due to its dedicated CPU allocation and minimal onboard disk, this server offers predictable compute density appropriate for web application serving, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and microservice infrastructure.
